headline: Village Farms books record cannabis sales as exports jump 75%
dek: Village Farms' Q3 cannabis sales hit a record $55M on European exports, while SNDL wins EU-GMP status for its Atholville site as wholesale flower prices fall.
key_points: Village Farms' cannabis sales rose 3% to a record $55.0 million in Q3, with international exports up 75% to $20.8 million.
Cannabis gross margin fell to 48% from 55% on weak Canadian wholesale trim prices, which management says hit bottom in Q3.
The company is mobilising its 30-acre Monahans, Texas greenhouse for cannabis and expects its Delta 2 expansion at full output by mid-2027.
SNDL said its Atholville, New Brunswick facility won EU-GMP certification on 4 November, adding another Canadian exporter to Europe.
body: Village Farms International reported record cannabis sales for the third quarter on 9 November, with exports to Europe now carrying a large share of the business. Cannabis net sales rose 3% to $55.0 million, and international export sales climbed 75% from a year earlier to $20.8 million, matching the second-quarter record.

The same day, SNDL said its Atholville, New Brunswick facility had received European Union Good Manufacturing Practice certification on 4 November. Taken together, the two announcements show Canadian growers leaning harder on Europe's medical markets just as wholesale prices there are falling.

Consolidated net sales were $67 million and net income was $10 million, or $0.08 a share, the company's sixth straight profitable quarter. Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations was $18.2 million, or 27% of sales. Operating cash flow was $9.5 million, and Village Farms ended September with about $80 million in cash and a net cash position of $41 million.

The cannabis segment was less rosy beneath the record. Gross margin fell to 48% from 55% a year earlier, and segment net income dropped to $7.8 million from $12.0 million. Segment adjusted EBITDA fell to $14.7 million, or 27% of sales, from $20.2 million, or 38%. The company blamed a softer spot market for trim in Canada's wholesale channel and higher operating costs to support growth. Chief executive Michael DeGiglio said he believes trim volumes and prices hit their low point in the third quarter and should start to normalise in the fourth, citing October orders and new supply contracts at stronger prices.

Exports made up about 43% of cannabis sales. Village Farms describes itself as one of the largest exporters of medical cannabis to Europe with a leading share in Germany, and says its prices abroad held up better than in parts of the supply chain without GMP certification.
## Capacity coming, and a Texas option

The company is adding supply on three fronts. Its Delta 2 greenhouse expansion in British Columbia is on track to finish in the first quarter of 2027 and reach 40 tonnes a year by mid-2027, taking the Delta campus to about 160 tonnes of dried flower annually. Its Groningen facility in the Netherlands is now fully planted after propagation work cut output in the quarter, and should reach full annual capacity in early 2027. It has also exercised rights that would let it convert 16 acres of its Delta 1 greenhouse to cannabis, though it has not formalised a plan.

In the United States, Village Farms has begun mobilising its standalone 30-acre greenhouse in Monahans, Texas for cannabis production, calling it the youngest and most advanced asset it owns. The company did not set out a licence route; it said it is pursuing all potential pathways to US market entry. Its CBD unit, Balanced Health Botanicals, is waiting for clarity on the federal hemp change due on 11 December before deciding how to pursue a Medicare pilot for CBD products.
> Europe has become the profit pool that Canadian oversupply could not provide. The question for 2027 is how many certified growers it can hold before prices give way.

SNDL's Atholville facility, previously owned by Zenabis, covers about 380,000 square feet with more than 110,000 square feet of canopy and capacity of roughly 4,500 kilograms a quarter, StratCann reported. SNDL says it could support more than 30 tonnes a year with targeted investment, and that lighting upgrades are under way. The certificate covers production and packaging of flower for regulated medical markets. SNDL's international sales rose from $3.8 million in the second quarter of 2025 to $5 million a year later, a small base next to Village Farms.

More certified supply is arriving as prices soften. The Fall 2026 Global Cannabis Report from the Global Cannabis Exchange found lower-end German wholesale flower prices down about 30% to 35% since spring, MMJDaily reported, with EU-GMP flower in Germany trading between €0.85 and €3.15 a gram depending on potency. The UK and Switzerland were the only markets in the report where prices did not fall. Village Farms' claim of resilient pricing for GMP product fits that picture: certification still earns a premium, but the premium is being tested. As we reported on 8 November, Aurora Cannabis also lifted export sales 44% on German and Polish demand.

Watch whether Village Farms' fourth-quarter margin recovers as management expects, and when Delta 2 and Groningen volumes start to show in export sales. Watch for SNDL to name European buyers for Atholville flower. And watch Germany's third-quarter import data and the fate of Berlin's proposed limits on telemedicine prescribing, which could shrink the market these growers are building for.
